correctness.rationale: For nonadjacent twin vertices u,v of any finite connected H with d common neighbors, the self-inclusive H-averaging matrix has antisymmetric eigenvector e_u-e_v with eigenvalue ρ=1/(d+1), so the initially dormant edge opinion difference is Dρ^t until activation; its confidence is cδ^t. The initial open ε-neighborhood ensures all H edges remain receptive by sup-norm contraction. Strict receptivity means exact critical equality never activates: δ≤ρ gives permanent nonreceptivity despite consensus, while δ>ρ gives first time floor(log(D/c)/log((d+1)δ))+1. Upon activation, full G averaging eliminates antisymmetric component in one step; perturbations remain ε-close and all confidences reinforce, so G stays fully receptive and consensus is reached. Independence tests explicitly stepped the real synchronous fractions for three-node H, including time-one equality, 81 assertions. The d=1 three-agent case and the almost-complete graph family were previously published; the claim is its extension to any connected twin-containing H with an open opinion neighborhood.
residual_risks: Unrestricted assertions rest on the analytic proofs, not finite checks.

evidence: The prior complete-network missing-dyad result has d=n-2; general H has arbitrary other vertices, edges and common-neighbor degree.

originality.rationale: Best-knowledge assessment against mathematically matching and broader prior claims; explicit boundaries and uninspected-source risks retained. A graph-local criterion based solely on twin degree for whether a dormant social tie ever regains receptivity despite eventual opinion consensus. It turns known qualitative adaptive-confidence behaviors into a sharp topology-independent phase transition with explicit first activation time and stability under perturbations.
